problem.title: The vicious cycle of the modern farmer
problem.subtitle: The more you fertilise synthetically, the more dependent you become. Soils lose their microbial life, plants weaken and your costs keep rising. There's another way.

items.title: Costs that keep rising
items.desc: Fertilisers, pesticides, tillage… more expensive every year, with shrinking margins.

items.title: Increasingly inert soils
items.desc: Intensive mechanisation and herbicides destroy the microbial fauna that makes the land fertile.

items.title: Dependence on external inputs
items.desc: Every season relying on suppliers, global prices and supply chains you don't control.

items.title: Uncertainty in the face of climate
items.desc: Droughts, resistant pests, irregular seasons… without soil resilience, every event becomes a crisis.

problem.quote: Fertility cannot be bought. It must be cultivated, understood and returned to the soil.
problem.quoteAuthor: Carles Pons — Founder of Bosque Madre

seo.title: The Programme — Suelos Vivos
seo.description: Three in-person workshops plus 12 months of biofertility and regenerative agriculture coaching. 2026–2027 programme in Tormos, Alicante. Only 20 places.

hero.title: Twelve months.
hero.subtitle: Suelos Vivos is an annual training and mentoring programme designed for professional farmers who want to learn to understand their farm as a living, productive ecosystem, by activating their soil's biology and applying biofertility techniques to cut costs and gain in quality.

items.label: In-person workshops
items.desc: Full weekends in Tormos (Alicante). Theory and field practice with materials included.

items.label: Months of coaching
items.desc: Monthly online sessions between workshops. Questions answered, plan adjusted, personalised follow-up.

items.label: Places per edition
items.desc: Small groups to ensure personalised attention and peer learning. No waiting list.

items.title: Living soil: diagnosis and foundations
items.desc: The first workshop lays the groundwork. You will learn to understand the soil as a living ecosystem, identify its health indicators and diagnose the state of your farm before intervening.
topics: Soil biology: fungi, bacteria, soil fauna and their roles
Nutrient cycles mediated by microorganisms
How to read a soil analysis (and what it doesn't tell you)
Visual and sensory indicators of soil health
Practical field diagnosis: your soil has a history
Introduction to applied regenerative principles
Permanent cover crops (I)
Techniques for capturing and multiplying local microorganisms

items.title: Biofertility in practice
items.desc: The second workshop is the most hands-on. Together we will produce the main bioinputs: inoculants, broths and activated compost. All using accessible materials reproducible on your farm.
topics: Microbial inoculants: production and application
Advanced composting with biological activators
Foliar and soil biofertilisation: when and how
Protocols adapted to different crops and climates
Theory and practice of biofertilisers
Biochar, rock dust, bokashi

items.title: Autonomy and plan design
items.desc: The third workshop closes the cycle. You will design your own biofertility plan for the next 3 years, evaluate the first year's results and map the route to technical autonomy.
topics: Evaluating results: how to measure soil improvement
Permanent cover crops (II)
Biofertility plan, case studies
Long-term water and organic matter management
Cost calculation and real economic impact
Roadmap: the next 3 years on your farm
Theory and practice of biofertilisers (II)
Mineral broths and natural biostimulants

workshops.note: *Note: the workshop content is much broader and will be adapted as far as possible to the group's specific needs.

items.title: Monthly online sessions
items.desc: Three-hour sessions each month without a workshop to review progress, resolve technical questions and adjust the plan to what is happening on your farm.

items.title: Private participant group
items.desc: A direct channel between all participants. To share results, experiences and mutual support among farmers.

items.title: Resource library
items.desc: Protocols, technical sheets, videos and selected bibliography. Fully accessible during and after the programme.

seo.title: About Us — Suelos Vivos
seo.description: Suelos Vivos is the training project of Bosque Madre: over 15 years of regenerative agriculture in the Mediterranean, with Carles Pons as lead trainer.

hero.title:
Born from the field.
Not the office.
hero.subtitle: We are a group of people driven by one mission: to regenerate agricultural ecosystems and give everyone access to healthy, quality food, while protecting the most important thing agriculture and society have — fertile soil.

paragraphs: Suelos Vivos comes from years of study, practice and direct observation in the field. From visiting holdings, supporting regeneration processes and seeing how many productive systems lose fertility while growing more dependent on external inputs.

This project turns that experience into training, advisory work and community for farmers who want to recover life in their soil, autonomy in their decisions and their own judgement in managing fertility.
We are not a company of agronomists here to hand out recipes, but to drive a movement of organic agriculture built on empowering farmers as masters of the fertility of their own crops.
intro.imgAlt: The Suelos Vivos team at the farm in Tormos, Alicante

story.title: Over 15 years transforming soils in the Mediterranean
paragraphs: Suelos Vivos was born from a simple question: is it possible to produce quality food, cut costs and improve the soil at the same time?

The answer, after years of experimentation, is yes. But it takes a change of approach: seeing the soil not as an inert support to which nutrients are added, but as a living ecosystem that has to be understood and that, when it works well, fertilises, protects and sustains the crop.
We have spent more than 15 years practising, documenting and teaching these techniques.
Suelos Vivos is the distillation of all that learning: a programme designed so that professional farmers can walk the same path, with guidance and real results.

items.title: Real practice
items.desc: We don't teach an abstract method: we work from direct experience with soil, crops, water, organic matter and bio-inputs.

items.title: Reading the system
items.desc: Before intervening, we set out to understand the context: climate, soil, management, resources, limitations and production goals.

items.title: The farmer's autonomy
items.desc: The aim is not to create dependency, but for each participant to learn to make better decisions about the fertility of their own system.

trainer.name: Carles Pons
trainer.role: Founder of Bosque Madre and Suelos Vivos
trainer.bio: For two decades he has worked in soil regeneration, biofertility and agroecological design, combining field practice, teaching and outreach. He has worked as a trainer or as part of training teams in more than 20 countries, has taught dozens of courses for agricultural bodies, cooperatives and local councils, and has trained alongside international authorities in the field. His work also includes editing and translating books, producing documentaries and building networks around regenerative agriculture.
areas: Managing organic matter, cover crops and functional biodiversity

items.q: Who is Suelos Vivos for?
items.a: Suelos Vivos is designed for farmers, technicians, farms and projects that want to improve soil fertility, reduce their dependence on external inputs and move towards more regenerative, self-reliant management.

items.q: If I am a beginner, can I take part?
items.a: Yes. The programme combines clear fundamentals, applied practice and ongoing support. You do not need to know everything before starting, but you do need a genuine interest in applying what you learn.

items.q: Does the programme work for organic, conventional or transitioning farms?
items.a: Yes. The approach can be applied to organic and conventional farms as well as those in transition. The aim is to improve soil life and make more informed decisions, whatever your starting point.

items.q: Do I need to have a professional farm or crop?
items.a: Not necessarily. The programme is aimed especially at professional farmers and projects, but it can also be useful for anyone interested in regenerating agricultural soils.

items.q: Will these techniques work in my climate, soil or crop?
items.a: The principles of biofertility and soil regeneration are universal and applicable in many contexts, but they always need adapting to the climate, soil type, crop, available resources and objectives of each farm.

items.q: What makes Suelos Vivos different from a conventional course?
items.a: This programme is not just a one-off training. It is a programme of learning, support and community, designed to help you apply what you learn in your own system.

items.q: How is the annual programme organised?
items.a: The programme combines in-person workshops, online follow-up sessions, digital materials, a private community and personalised support to help you build a roadmap adapted to your farm or project.

items.q: What happens between workshops?
items.a: Between workshops the process continues through online meetings, practical assignments, answering questions and following each participant's progress.

items.q: How does the Suelos Vivos community work?
items.a: The community is a private space to share progress, questions, experiences and learning with other participants who are on a similar path.

items.q: Do I need to bring soil analyses, samples or information about my farm?
items.a: We recommend bringing as much information as possible: photographs, soil or water analyses, management data, crops, recurring problems and objectives. The better we understand your context, the more useful the support will be.

items.q: What is a biofactory?
items.a: A biofactory is a concept for setting up a space to produce bio-inputs, ferments, microbiological preparations and fertility tools that reduce costs and dependence on external products.

items.q: What kind of results can I expect?
items.a: The aim is for you to understand your soil better, to build and put into practice a plan to improve fertility, cut unnecessary costs and make better-informed decisions. Concrete results will depend on your starting point, your management and how it is actually applied on each farm.

items.q: What if I see no results by the end of the course?
items.a: Soil regeneration is a gradual process. The programme is designed to give you tools, follow-up and the judgement to interpret what is happening and adjust management when needed. If you follow the programme, results will come — sometimes quickly and directly, sometimes gradually.

items.q: What if I cannot attend one of the in-person workshops?
items.a: If you cannot attend a workshop, we will find the best way for you not to lose the thread of the programme through materials, recordings or online follow-up, depending on the specific conditions of that edition. If you are short of time, we offer two alternatives: booking a personalised advisory service or waiting for the fully online programme.

items.q: When will the online edition of Suelos Vivos be available?
items.a: An online edition is planned for spring 2027, for those who cannot travel or prefer to follow the programme remotely.

items.q: What if I cannot attend a live online session?
items.a: Whenever possible, sessions will be recorded or materials provided so you can follow the content even if you could not join live.

items.q: How long will I have access to the materials and the community?
items.a: Access to materials and community depends on the specific conditions of each edition. For this first edition we are offering lifetime access to the online materials and to the soil regeneration community.

items.q: Do I get a certificate at the end of the programme?
items.a: Yes, a certificate of participation or completion is planned for those who complete the training according to the established conditions.

items.q: Are accommodation, meals or transport included?
items.a: In principle, accommodation, meals and transport are not included unless stated otherwise in the specific information for each workshop or edition.

items.q: Can I cancel once the programme has started?
items.a: Yes, it is possible. Cancellation terms depend on the enrolment format, the deposit and the payment method. We recommend reviewing the specific conditions before confirming your place.

items.q: Is instalment payment or financing available?
items.a: Yes. Instalment payment and other arrangements are planned depending on the edition and the enrolment conditions. Details are provided before the booking is confirmed.
